title: Caching Strategies
description: Understand different caching strategies and their tradeoffs.

options.text: Write-through cache has higher write latency but ensures cache consistency
options.explanation: Write-through writes to both cache and database synchronously. Higher write latency (two writes) but cache always has latest data. Good for read-heavy workloads where consistency matters.

options.text: Cache-aside (lazy loading) prevents cache stampede by default
options.explanation: Cache-aside is vulnerable to cache stampede — when a popular key expires, many requests simultaneously hit the database. Stampede protection (mutex locks, probabilistic early expiry) must be added explicitly.

options.text: Write-behind cache guarantees zero data loss
options.explanation: Write-behind (write-back) buffers writes and flushes asynchronously. If the cache node crashes before flushing, buffered writes are lost. It trades durability for write performance.

options.text: TTL-based expiry is the only way to invalidate cached data
options.explanation: Other strategies include explicit invalidation (delete on write), event-driven invalidation (pub/sub), and versioned keys. TTL is the simplest but can serve stale data.
